question: President Zelenskyy said, in the presence of Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni, that he would draw up a list of ‘Putin fans in Italy’ and that the Italian Government should ‘revoke their visas and expel them’. Ukraine has already set up a proscription website – myrotvorets.center1 – run by its Security Service.

The site publishes the names and addresses of ‘enemies of Ukraine’ (given that label if they have opinions that diverge from the government line). Among those blacklisted were Ukrainian writer Oles Buzina and former member of parliament Oleh Kalašnikov, who were both murdered. No one has been convicted in either case.

As far back as 2016, the site published the personal data of 4 508 journalists and other media staff around the world. The European Parliament has called for the site to be shut down2, yet Ukraine’s Secret Service considers its activities to be lawful3. In view of the above: 1.
Does the Commission believe that the statements by the Ukrainian President are acceptable?
Does it not see them as a clear attempt to intimidate and indirectly threaten people in Italy who disagree with the government’s foreign policy concerning the war in Ukraine?
answer: The statements were given in the context of bilateral relations between Italy and Ukraine. With regard to visa policy, it is a competence of Member States to examine and decide on visa applications. The disclosure of personal data of EU citizens without their consent has been raised with Ukrainian counterparts on several occasions.
We continue to call on the Ukrainian authorities to undertake the necessary steps to avoid any illegal disclosure of personal data.

In the Commission Communication on EU Enlargement policy from 8 November 2023 (4), Ukraine is encouraged to continue working on alignment with the EU acquis, including on personal data protection, to meet the requirements of both the Council of Europe Convention 108+ for the protection of individuals with regard to the processing of personal dat a (5) and the General Data Protection Regulation (6).
